raw_text:
Thanks for the clear brief. Here’s a 12-week, cycle-aware strength program for a 28-year-old recreational lifter with primary dysmenorrhea. The plan phases around her 28-day cycle, with lighter, low-Valsalva and no high-impact work during days 1–3 of menses, and full training outside that window. The text assumes the next cycle starts around 2026-06-01 (cycle day 1). If her actual dates shift, you can map the cycle days accordingly.

Structure overview
- Cycle-aware approach: Each four-week block aligns with cycle days:
  - Week 1: Cycle days 1–7 (start of menses; Week 1 contains days 1–3 as the most symptomatic window; adjust daily)
  - Week 2: Cycle days 4–10
  - Week 3: Cycle days 11–17
  - Week 4: Cycle days 18–24
  - Then repeat for weeks 5–12 with the same cycle-day alignment.
- Training emphasis:
  - Outside days 1–3 of menses: progressive strength with compound lifts, controlled tempo, moderate to heavy loads.
  - Days 1–3 of menses: reduced intensity; avoid heavy Valsalva, no heavy load or high-impact jumps; cardio optional low intensity; maintain movement to support recovery.
- Weekly layout (example outside menses): 4 training days per week with 2–3 accessory days as needed.
- Reproductive health considerations: implement auto-regulation, RPE-based progressions, and ensure adequate rest. If symptoms worsen, shift to even lighter days or deload as needed.

Phase plan
- Phase A (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and neuromuscular efficiency; establish baseline strength, technique, and tolerable loading during menses and non-menses weeks.
- Phase B (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload with increased sets/reps and slightly higher loads; re-test strength at Week 4 and Week 8.
- Phase C (Weeks 9–12): Peak strength and planned volume cycling; test maxes via controlled 1RM estimates or rep max benchmarks then refine.

Cycle-day guided weekly skeleton
- For each week, assign 3–4 sessions. If Week 1 (menses) aligns with days 1–3, plan lighter sessions those days; otherwise, plan per actual calendar alignment.
- Training days outside days 1–3: aim for 3–4 sets per main lift, progressing load gradually.
- Mobility and conditioning: 10–20 min daily mobility; optional 1–2 low-impact cardio sessions per week (e.g., brisk walking, cycling 20–30 min).

Week-by-week plan (12 weeks)
Note: Replace calendar dates with cycle days if you track exact days. The plan follows the cycle: D1–D3 light, D4–D28 regular.

Weeks 1–4 (Phase A: Foundation)
- Week 1 (Cycle days 1–7)
  - Day 1 (menses, light): 
    - Squat 3x5 at 60–65% of estimated 1RM, tempo 3-1-1, RPE 5–6
    - HB RDL 3x8 at light load
    - Push press or dumbbell shoulder press 3x8
    - Core work: planks 3x45s; side planks 2x30s
    - Mobility 10–15 min
  - Day 2 (off or rehab): 
    - Hip hinge pattern work, glute activation (glute bridges, face pulls)
  - Day 3 (non-menses heavy lifting window should be used if days 4–7): 
    - Front squat 3x5 at 65–70%
    - Romanian deadlift 3x8
    - Bench press 3x6–8
    - Dumbbell rows 3x8
    - Accessory: triceps pushdown 3x12
  - Day 4 (conditioning/light): 
    - Mobility circuit 15 min; optional 15–20 min bike at light pace

- Week 2 (Cycle days 4–10)
  - Day 1: 
    - Back squat 4x4 at 70–75% 1RM
    - Barbell hip thrust 3x6
    - Overhead press 3x6
    - Pull-ups or lat pulldown 3x6–8
    - Core: dead bug 3x12 per side
  - Day 3: 
    - Romanian deadlift 4x6
    - Goblet squat 3x8
    - Incline bench press 3x8
    - Ring rows or lat pulldown 3x8
  - Day 4: 
    - Conditioning 20–25 min or tempo cardio 20 min
  - Optional: accessory arms/calves/core lightly

- Week 3 (Cycle days 11–17)
  - Day 1: 
    - Squat 4x5 at 72–78%
    - Deadlift 3x5 at 72–78%
    - Dumbbell bench press 4x6
  - Day 3:
    - Front squat 3x5
    - Deficit or tempo tempo deadlift 3x5
    - Bent-over row 3x6
  - Day 4: 
    - Mobility 15–20, light cardio 15–20

- Week 4 (Cycle days 18–24) Deload and technique focus
  - Day 1: 
    - Squat 3x5 at 60–65%
    - Romanian deadlift 3x6
    - Push press 3x6
  - Day 3:
    - Bench press 3x5
    - Barbell row 3x6
    - Lunges 3x8 per leg
  - Day 4:
    - Conditioning 15–20, mobility

Weeks 5–8 (Phase B: Progressive overload)
- Week 5 (Cycle days 1–7)
  - Day 1: 
    - Back squat 5x5 at 75–80%
    - Hip thrust 4x6
  - Day 2 (optional): 
    - Mobility work; light conditioning
  - Day 3: 
    - Deadlift 4x5 at 75%
    - Overhead press 4x6
  - Day 4: 
    - Bench press 4x6
- Week 6 (Cycle days 4–10)
  - Day 1: 
    - Squat 4x6 at 78–82%
    - Romanian deadlift 3x6
  - Day 3: 
    - Front squat 4x5
    - Barbell row 4x6
  - Day 4: 
    - Chins or lat pulldown 3x6
- Week 7 (Cycle days 11–17)
  - Day 1: 
    - Squat 5x5 at 80–85%
    - Hip thrust 4x6
  - Day 3: 
    - Deadlift 4x4 at 80–85%
    - Bench press 4x6
  - Day 4: 
    - Accessory circuit: hamstring curl, core
- Week 8 (Cycle days 18–24) Deload/technique
  - Similar to Week 4 with lighter loads (60–65% 1RM) and emphasis on form, tempo:

Weeks 9–12 (Phase C: Peak strength and testing)
- Week 9 (Cycle days 1–7)
  - Day 1: 
    - Squat 4x4 at 85% 1RM
    - Hip thrust 3x6
  - Day 3: 
    - Deadlift 3x4 at 85%
    - Overhead press 3x6
  - Day 4: 
    - Bench press 4x5
- Week 10 (Cycle days 4–10)
  - Day 1: 
    - Back squat 3x3 at 90%
    - Romanian deadlift 3x5
  - Day 3: 
    - Front squat 3x3 at 85–90%
    - Pendlay row 3x6
  - Day 4: 
    - Pull-ups or lat pulldown 3x6; accessory arms
- Week 11 (Cycle days 11–17)
  - Day 1: 
    - Squat 3x2 at 92–95%
    - Hip thrust 3x5
  - Day 3: 
    - Deadlift 3x2 at 92–95%
    - Bench press 3x4
  - Day 4: 
    - Mobility and light conditioning
- Week 12 (Cycle days 18–24) Peak testing and consolidation
  - Test days (optional but recommended)
    - 1RM estimates or 5RM for squat, bench, deadlift
    - If testing, use warm-up protocols and record PRs
  - Otherwise: 3–4 sets of heavy triples, then deload in following week if needed
  - Accessory work: 2–3 sets of core, glutes, and upper back

Exercise selection and substitutions
- Core lifts: Squat, deadlift, bench press, overhead press, row variations, hip hinge patterns.
- Substitutions: If a lift is painful, swap with a variation that preserves pattern (e.g., goblet squat for back squat, trap bar deadlift for conventional deadlift).
- Tempo cues: Emphasize control and stability, e.g., 3-1-1 tempo on eccentric, pause at bottom for 1 second where appropriate.
- Repetition ranges: 4–6 reps for strength blocks, 6–8 for hypertrophy emphasis, 8–12 for accessory work. Use RPE 6–9 depending on week and cycle day.

On cycle-day specifics
- Days 1–3 of menses (cycle day 1–3): 
  - Reduce intensity by about 10–30% if pain is high; avoid maximal loads and Valsalva-heavy lifting.
  - Keep main lifts at 3x5 or 3x6 with light to moderate loads and longer rest (2–3 minutes); focus on technique, activation, and controlled breathing.
  - If symptoms are particularly debilitating, swap to: leg accessory work, core, mobility, and light cardio under supervision.
- Days 4–28:
  - Normal progression with 4–5 day splits as described; adjust loads based on how the client feels.

Nutrition and recovery
- Caloric stance: Maintain a slight caloric surplus for strength gains if goal is appreciable hypertrophy and strength; approximate 250–500 kcal above maintenance depending on body weight and activity level.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day to support muscle repair and growth.
- Carbohydrates: Align with training load; higher around more intense sessions to support performance.
- Hydration: 2–3 L daily baseline; increase on high-intensity days.
- Recovery modalities: 7–9 hours sleep, 15–20 minutes of daily mobility work, light cardio on non-lifting days to aid recovery.
- Dysmenorrhea management considerations:
  - Consider NSAID timing if advised by doctor, but avoid routine use before workouts without medical clearance.
  - Gentle breathing, mindfulness, and low-impact cardio during menstrual days can reduce perceived exertion.
  - Heating pad or warm baths can alleviate pelvic discomfort; if heavy cramping, schedule more rest or deload.

Progression rules
- Add small increments when the prescribed reps and sets were completed with good form and RPE around 7–8.
- If form breaks or pain arises, reduce weight by 5–10% and/or switch to a less technical variation.
- Use auto-regulation: if a given week feels tough, stick to the lower end of the prescribed ranges and consolidate progress.

Notes for the trainer
- Track cycle day, RPE, loads, and any symptoms weekly to tailor the plan.
- Keep an emphasis on technique and form, especially when approaching higher loads in Weeks 9–12.
- Communicate openly about symptoms; be ready to swap sessions if needed, especially during days 1–3 of menses.

If you’d like, I can map this into a calendar with specific dates, set/reps for each session per week, and provide a printable template for your client.
